+# Finite Fibers Preserve Topological Entropy
+
+## Abstract
+
+A compact factor map with a uniform bound on its finite fibers preserves topological entropy.
+
+Let X and Y be compact uniform spaces, with Y Hausdorff. Let S:X→X be continuous, and let π:X→Y be a continuous surjection satisfying π∘S=T∘π. Every fiber π⁻¹{y} is finite and its cardinality is at most the same natural number M. The covering entropy of S equals that of T. This formalizes the classical finite-to-one factor theorem; no literature novelty is claimed.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Entropy equality under uniformly finite fibers).**
+
+$$\begin{aligned}\forall X: Type, \forall Y: Type,\\{[\operatorname{UniformSpace}(X)] [\operatorname{CompactSpace}(X)] [\operatorname{UniformSpace}(Y)] [\operatorname{CompactSpace}(Y)] [\operatorname{T2Space}(Y)],}\\\forall S: X \to X, \forall T: Y \to Y, \forall \pi: X \to Y,\\\operatorname{Continuous}(S) \Rightarrow \operatorname{Continuous}(\pi) \Rightarrow\\\operatorname{Function.Surjective}(\pi) \Rightarrow \operatorname{Function.Semiconj}(\pi, S, T) \Rightarrow\\\forall M: \mathbb{N},\\{\forall y: Y, \operatorname{Set.Finite}(\operatorname{Set.preimage}(\pi, \operatorname{Set.singleton}(y))) \land \operatorname{Set.ncard}(\operatorname{Set.preimage}(\pi, \operatorname{Set.singleton}(y))) \le M} \Rightarrow\\\operatorname{Dynamics.coverEntropy}(S, \operatorname{Set.univ}()) = \operatorname{Dynamics.coverEntropy}(T, \operatorname{Set.univ}())\end{aligned}$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Dynamics/FiniteFiberEntropy.finite_fiber_entropy` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Rufus Bowen (1971). *Entropy for group endomorphisms and homogeneous spaces*. DOI: [10.1090/S0002-9947-1971-0274707-X](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9947-1971-0274707-X). URL: <https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9947-1971-0274707-X>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For a symmetric source entourage U and fixed block length n, the n-step balls centered on a fiber cover that fiber using at most M centers. Since π is a closed map, this cover extends to the inverse image of a neighborhood of the base point. The Lebesgue number lemma makes the base entourage uniform over Y.
+
+Over r consecutive blocks, each base covering orbit has at most M^r center codes. One actual orbit representative from every nonempty code class gives a source cover at entourage U∘U. No continuous selection of fiber points or lifting of a prescribed orbit is assumed. The source covering number at time n*r is at most M^r times the base covering number. Monotonicity permits restriction to these multiples; their extra entropy is log(M)/n, which tends to zero.
+
+The reverse inequality reuses Mathlib's coverEntropy_image_le_of_uniformContinuous. The proof handles empty spaces, M=0 when both spaces are empty, and infinite entropy. It does not require T to be continuous or X to be Hausdorff. Finiteness of fibers is an explicit hypothesis: Set.ncard alone cannot express a finite bound because it is zero on an infinite set. The result supplies the entropy comparison needed by finite symbolic codings of compact dynamical systems; constructing a coding and proving its uniform fiber bound remain application-specific obligations.
+

+# The all-index denominator formula for OEIS A362534
+
+## Abstract
+
+For every positive index, the reduced denominator of the polarization-transfer ratio is the odd binomial gap divided by its greatest common divisor with the ceiling half-index.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Exact reduced fractions for every positive index).**
+
+$$\forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall m \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall B \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall v \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall b \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall G \in \mathbb{N},\; (1 \le n \land \left(m = n - \operatorname{NatDiv}\left(n, 2\right) \land \left(B = \operatorname{choose}\left(n, \operatorname{NatDiv}\left(n, 2\right)\right) \land \left(v = \operatorname{factorization}\left(B, 2\right) \land \left(b = \operatorname{NatDiv}\left(B, 2^{v}\right) \land G = \operatorname{NatDiv}\left(2^{n} - B, 2^{v}\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{num}\left(\operatorname{g}\left(n\right)\right) = G \land \left(\operatorname{den}\left(\frac{\operatorname{f}\left(n\right)}{\operatorname{g}\left(n\right)}\right) = \operatorname{NatDiv}\left(G, \operatorname{gcd}\left(m, G\right)\right) \land \operatorname{num}\left(\frac{\operatorname{f}\left(n\right)}{\operatorname{g}\left(n\right)}\right) = \operatorname{NatDiv}\left(m \cdot b, \operatorname{gcd}\left(m, G\right)\right)\right))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/FactorialRatio/DyadicBinomialCancellation.denominator_formula` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The functions f and g are the original rational-valued OEIS formulas from SabbaPolarizationTransferRefutation. For n at least one, let k be floor(n/2), m = n-k, B = choose(n,k), v the exponent of two in B, b = B/2^v and G = (2^n-B)/2^v. Then num(g) = G, den(f/g) = G/gcd(m,G), and num(f/g) = mb/gcd(m,G). The proof derives B strictly between zero and 2^n, hence v < n, positive odd b and G, and coprimality of b and G. The binomial identity n choose(n-1,k) = mB connects the normalized ratio to the original parity definitions. These are exact unbounded arithmetic statements, including n = 1 and n = 2. They do not formalize the physical derivation of either bound. This is the formalization of an existing written correction, not an additional claim of mathematical novelty or a new finite computation.
+

+        return Disp(result);

+# Native positive-SMALL chain extraction
+
+## Abstract
+
+Every negative physical label in an actual positive-SMALL centered source starts a dyadic chain with exact seed transport.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (A dyadic chain from each negative occurrence).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Circle/NativeSeedChains.native_chain_extraction`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Circle/NativeSeedChains.native_chain_extraction` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let k>=3, t be any natural number, N=2^k-1, Q=2^(k-2), and w=SourceWidth.actualSource(k,t) on physical labels Fin(k). Assume every label with |w(i)|<Q has w(i)>0. For any negative label n, take its physical successor as the seed label and write a for that seed's value. A finite literal forward path of SMALL labels starts at that seed label and ends immediately before a positive LARGE root p. Its values are a,2a,...,p/2; the path may be empty. The chain, including its root and following negative label, has no repeated physical label and has length at most k. The following physical labels have values -B=2p-N and b=4p-N. The root satisfies Q<=p and 3p<=N; both seeds a and b are positive and congruent to 1 modulo 4.
+
+Writing s for the SMALL mass and d=B-p, the chain has s=p-a, d>=0 and s-d=b-a. +# Deferred-prefix ancestor invariant
+
+## Abstract
+
+Appending a dyadic list and retaining its affordable prefix preserves ancestor heights and bounds the peak at a first omission.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Physical splitting, exact landing and the ancestor range).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Circle/SeedQueueInvariant.deferred_prefix_invariant`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Circle/SeedQueueInvariant.deferred_prefix_invariant` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Weights f are integers on arbitrary physical labels. A queue has ancestor range [0,D] relative to mu if, for each occurrence q, its value minus mu minus the mass preceding that occurrence lies in [0,D]. Equal values do not identify occurrences. Assume the old queue has this ancestor range and mu<=b. Append a dyadic list with seed a. If that list is nonempty, assume its birth height a-mu-mass(old) lies in [0,D]. Each appended dyadic occurrence has exactly that birth height; retaining an initial segment preserves the preceding mass of each retained occurrence.
+
+The recursive splitBudget consumes labels from the front while the next weight fits the remaining budget. It returns a literal prefix q and literal suffix e of old++small, with mass(q)<=b-mu. For positive weights this is the longest affordable initial segment. Set oldHeight=a-mu-mass(old). With native transport mass(small)-(B-p)=b-a and 2(C-B)=b-1, the postnegative height is h=b-mu-mass(q)>=0, and direct mass conservation gives oldHeight+mass(e)+p-B=h. If x is the first emitted label, maximality gives b-mu<mass(q)+f(x). Its remembered ancestor height delta=f(x)-mu-mass(q) lies in [0,D], implying h<f(x) and B+h<=C+floor(D/2). If e is empty, the peak is exactly oldHeight+p. If b=mu and every input weight is positive, the retained queue is empty and the landing height is zero, so every currently available occurrence is emitted.
+
+The arithmetic and ancestor step itself does not require positive weights; positivity is needed to interpret the split as the longest affordable prefix, to force an empty queue at final zero budget, and to control intermediate positive heights. This local theorem has no supplied completion word or recovery witness. It does not by itself derive native seed extrema, partition the native source, iterate the queue through all chains, or recover the complete inventory. NativeSeedChains supplies individual native transport chains. A full source-coupled adaptive-width theorem and the original exact-C objective remain open.

+# Original integer scalar insertion transpose
+
+## Abstract
+
+NormalScalarTranspose
+
+The carrier is the original finite-charge direct sum of complex oscillator polynomials. B is complex bilinear, with its input order retained. No half-current or tensor carrier, symmetry, nondegeneracy, positivity, rank restriction, or all-source invariance is assumed. The normal product and divided derivative retain the Carnahan/native adaptation attribution of FieldNormalProduct. This is a classical finite normal-order calculation; no literature novelty is claimed.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (insertion).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/SourceBPZ/NormalScalarTranspose.insertion`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/SourceBPZ/NormalScalarTranspose.insertion` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every lattice D, coordinate i, natural derivative order p and actual vertex operator F, insertion is the actual normalMinusOne of dividedDerivative p (neutralField D i) with F. Thus its source oscillator is h_i(-(p+1)); it is not a newly reflected field.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (consumed_normal_product_form).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/SourceBPZ/NormalScalarTranspose.consumed_normal_product_form`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/SourceBPZ/NormalScalarTranspose.consumed_normal_product_form` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Fix arbitrary D, a complex bilinear B on Carrier D, a coordinate i, derivative order p, actual tail field F, an arbitrary label type with finite subset S, actual fields G(a), complex coefficients lambda(a), integer reflection constants K(a), and complex charge kappa. Assume B(h_i(k)x,y)=-B(x,h_i(-k)y) for every integer k and both inputs; B(F[t]x,y)=sum over a in S of lambda(a) B(x,G(a)[K(a)-t]y) for all t,x,y; and h_i(0)G(a)[t]x=G(a)[t]h_i(0)x+kappa G(a)[t]x for a in S. The tail premise concerns F only and assumes no normal-product transpose.
+
+For every integer m and inputs u,v, B(insertion(p,F)[m]u,v) equals (-1)^(p+1) times the sum over a in S of lambda(a) multiplied by: the sum over s=0,...,p of choose(p+1,s+1) B(u,insertion(s,G(a))[K(a)+p+s+2-m]v), plus kappa B(u,G(a)[K(a)+p+1-m]v). Equivalently n=p+1 and r=s+1 range through n>=1 and 1<=r<=n. The final term deletes the oscillator and never invokes a derivative of order -1.
+
+The actual constructor's two vector sums have finite support before scalar evaluation. With A=vectorFrequencyBound(u)+1 and C=vectorFrequencyBound(v)+1 the scalar intervals are k=1-C,...,-1 and k=0,...,A-1. The omitted derivative band -p<=k<0 has zero integer choose(-k-1,p). Finite reflection j=-k and integer Vandermonde give -choose(j-1,p)=(-1)^(p+1) sum over s=0,...,p of choose(p+1,s+1)choose(-j-1,s). Only the j=0 ordering boundary uses the charge covariance and produces the displayed kappa term.
+
+The consumer is the cons step of the original wordField BPZ induction: F is the tail wordField, G(a) are the finite lowered or deleted tail words, K(a) their exact opposite-mode constants, and kappa is bilinear(unitCharge i,alpha). At p=0 a singleton primary tail gives the nonprimary correction B(u,G[K+1-m]v) with coefficient -lambda*kappa. This unit does not construct the original pairing or charged-primary law, prove the word induction or permutation bridge, assemble the finite L1 source flow, or establish full VOA, CFT, fusion, string theory or AdS/CFT.

+/-!
+The classical finite-to-one entropy theorem is formalized without a novelty
+claim. The missing content, fixed before compilation, is the reverse cover
+bound: local length-n covers of each fiber extend to base neighborhoods,
+and one representative per realized block code gives at most M^r lifts of
+each base cover orbit of length n*r. No pointwise lifting or continuous
+choice is assumed. Multiples of n suffice by monotonicity of covering
+numbers. Their extra growth is log(M)/n, tending to zero.
+
+The final theorem includes empty spaces and infinite entropy. Finiteness
+of fibers is explicit, since Nat.card or Set.ncard alone vanishes on an
+infinite set. The helpers below are consumed by the final theorem.
+-/
+
+noncomputable section

+open scoped Topology Uniformity ENNReal SetRel
+
+namespace D5.S1.Dynamics.FiniteFiberEntropy
+
+variable {X Y : Type*}
+
+private lemma local_block_covers
+    [UniformSpace X] [CompactSpace X]
+    [UniformSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] [T2Space Y]
+    (π : X → Y) (hπ : Continuous π) (S : X → X) (hS : Continuous S)
+    (M : ℕ)
+    (hfib : ∀ y, (π ⁻¹' {y}).Finite ∧ (π ⁻¹' {y}).ncard ≤ M)
+    (U : SetRel X X) (hU : U ∈ 𝓤 X) [U.IsSymm] (n : ℕ) :
+    ∃ V ∈ 𝓤 Y, ∀ y, ∃ s : Finset X,
+      s.card ≤ M ∧ IsDynCoverOf S (π ⁻¹' UniformSpace.ball y V) U n s := by
+  classical
+  let A : Y → Set Y := fun q =>
+    {q' | ∀ x ∈ π ⁻¹' {q'},
+      ∃ z ∈ π ⁻¹' {q}, (z, x) ∈ dynEntourage S U n}
+  have hA (q : Y) : A q ∈ 𝓝 q := by
+    apply hπ.isClosedMap.eventually_nhds_fiber q
+    intro z hz
+    filter_upwards [ball_dynEntourage_mem_nhds hS hU n z] with x hx
+    exact ⟨z, hz, hx⟩

+/- The missing counting step: choose one actual orbit per realized block code.
+The centers of a block need not lift the center of the base orbit. The code
+construction follows Mathlib's Dynamics.IsDynCoverOf.iterate_le_pow. -/
+private theorem block_cover_lift {X Y : Type*} [Nonempty X]
+    (S : X → X) (T : Y → Y) (π : X → Y) (hπ : Semiconj π S T)
+    (U : SetRel X X) [U.IsSymm] (V : SetRel Y Y) [V.IsSymm]
+    (M n r : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)
+    (hloc : ∀ y, ∃ c : Finset X, c.card ≤ M ∧
+      IsDynCoverOf S (π ⁻¹' UniformSpace.ball y V) U n c)
+    (b : Finset Y) (hb : IsDynCoverOf T univ V (n * r) b) :
+    ∃ a : Finset X, IsDynCoverOf S univ (U ○ U) (n * r) a ∧
+      a.card ≤ b.card * M ^ r := by
+  classical
+  choose c hc_card hc using hloc
+  let Code := (y : b) × ((k : Fin r) → c (T^[n * k.val] y.val))
+  let cell (w : Code) : Set X :=
+    {x | ∀ k : Fin r,
+      (S^[n * k.val] x, (w.2 k).val) ∈ dynEntourage S U n}
+  let representative (w : Code) : X :=
+    if h : (cell w).Nonempty then h.choose else Classical.arbitrary X
+  have hrep (w : Code) (x : X) (hx : x ∈ cell w) : representative w ∈ cell w := by
+    have h : (cell w).Nonempty := ⟨x, hx⟩
+    simpa only [representative, dite_eq_left h] using h.choose_spec
+  let a : Finset X := Finset.univ.image representative
+  refine ⟨a, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro x _
+    obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := hb (mem_univ (π x))
+    have hblock (k : Fin r) :
+        S^[n * k.val] x ∈ π ⁻¹' UniformSpace.ball (T^[n * k.val] y) V := by
+      change (T^[n * k.val] y, π (S^[n * k.val] x)) ∈ V
+      rw [(hπ.iterate_right (n * k.val)) x]
+      exact V.symm ((mem_dynEntourage.mp hxy) (n * k.val) (Nat.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left k.isLt hn))
+    have hchoose (k : Fin r) : ∃ z : c (T^[n * k.val] y),
+        (S^[n * k.val] x, z.val) ∈ dynEntourage S U n := by
+      obtain ⟨z, hz, hxz⟩ := hc (T^[n * k.val] y) (hblock k)
+      exact ⟨⟨z, hz⟩, hxz⟩
+    choose z hz using hchoose
+    let w : Code := ⟨⟨y, hy⟩, z⟩
+    have hx : x ∈ cell w := hz
+    have hycell := hrep w x hx
+    refine ⟨representative w, Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨w, Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
+    apply mem_dynEntourage.mpr
+    intro i hi
+    let k : Fin r := ⟨i / n, Nat.div_lt_of_lt_mul (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using hi)⟩
+    have hix := mem_dynEntourage.mp (hx k) (i % n) (Nat.mod_lt i hn)
+    have hiy := mem_dynEntourage.mp (hycell k) (i % n) (Nat.mod_lt i hn)
+    have he : i % n + n * k.val = i := Nat.mod_add_div i n
+    rw [← iterate_add_apply, he] at hix hiy
+    exact ⟨_, hix, U.symm hiy⟩
+  · refine Finset.card_image_le.trans ?_
+    simp only [Finset.card_univ, Code, Fintype.card_sigma, Fintype.card_pi,
+      Fintype.card_coe]
+    calc
+      _ ≤ ∑ _y : b, M ^ r := Finset.sum_le_sum fun y _ => by
+        calc
+          _ ≤ ∏ _k : Fin r, M := Finset.prod_le_prod fun k _ => hc_card _
+          _ = _ := by simp
+      _ = b.card * M ^ r := by simp
+

+/-- Arbitrarily long blocks with a uniformly bounded branching cost do not
+increase covering entropy.  No nonemptiness or finiteness-of-entropy
+assumption is needed; `EReal` handles all endpoint cases. -/
+private lemma entropy_le_of_block_bound
+    {X Y : Type*} [UniformSpace X] [UniformSpace Y]
+    (S : X → X) (T : Y → Y) (U : SetRel X X)
+    (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M)
+    (hbound : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → ∃ V : SetRel Y Y, V ∈ 𝓤 Y ∧
+      ∀ r : ℕ, coverMincard S univ U (n * r) ≤
+        (M : ℕ∞) ^ r * coverMincard T univ V (n * r)) :
+    coverEntropyEntourage S univ U ≤ coverEntropy T univ := by
+  have hlog_bot : ENNReal.log (M : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ ⊥ := by
+    intro h
+    have hzero : (M : ℝ≥0∞) = 0 := ENNReal.log_eq_bot_iff.mp h
+    exact hM.ne' (by exact_mod_cast hzero)
+  have hlog_top : ENNReal.log (M : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ ⊤ := by simp
+  have hmonoS : Monotone (fun k => (coverMincard S univ U k).toENNReal) :=
+    fun _ _ h => ENat.toENNReal_mono (coverMincard_monotone_time S univ U h)
+  have happrox (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
+      coverEntropyEntourage S univ U ≤
+        ENNReal.log (M : ℝ≥0∞) / n + coverEntropy T univ := by
+    obtain ⟨V, hV, hb⟩ := hbound n hn
+    have hmonoT : Monotone (fun k => (coverMincard T univ V k).toENNReal) :=
+      fun _ _ h => ENat.toENNReal_mono (coverMincard_monotone_time T univ V h)
+    have hcost : expGrowthSup (fun r : ℕ => (M : ℝ≥0∞) ^ r) =
+        ENNReal.log (M : ℝ≥0∞) := expGrowthSup_pow
+    have hproduct :
+        expGrowthSup (fun r => (coverMincard S univ U (n * r)).toENNReal) ≤
+        ENNReal.log (M : ℝ≥0∞) +
+          expGrowthSup (fun r => (coverMincard T univ V (n * r)).toENNReal) := by
+      calc
+        _ ≤ expGrowthSup
+            ((fun r : ℕ => (M : ℝ≥0∞) ^ r) *
+              (fun r : ℕ => (coverMincard T univ V (n * r)).toENNReal)) := by
+          apply expGrowthSup_monotone
+          intro r
+          simpa only [Pi.mul_apply, ENat.toENNReal_mul, ENat.toENNReal_pow,
+            ENat.toENNReal_coe] using ENat.toENNReal_mono (hb r)
+        _ ≤ _ := by
+          have hp := expGrowthSup_mul_le
+            (u := fun r : ℕ => (M : ℝ≥0∞) ^ r)
+            (v := fun r : ℕ => (coverMincard T univ V (n * r)).toENNReal)
+            (Or.inl (hcost.symm ▸ hlog_bot)) (Or.inl (hcost.symm ▸ hlog_top))
+          simpa only [hcost] using hp
+    have hs := hmonoS.expGrowthSup_comp_mul hn.ne'
+    rw [mul_comm, ← EReal.div_eq_iff (EReal.natCast_ne_bot n)
+      (EReal.natCast_ne_top n) (Nat.cast_ne_zero.2 hn.ne')] at hs
+    change expGrowthSup (fun k => (coverMincard S univ U k).toENNReal) ≤ _
+    rw [← hs]
+    calc
+      _ ≤ (ENNReal.log (M : ℝ≥0∞) +
+          expGrowthSup (fun r => (coverMincard T univ V (n * r)).toENNReal)) / n :=
+        EReal.monotone_div_right_of_nonneg n.cast_nonneg' hproduct
+      _ = ENNReal.log (M : ℝ≥0∞) / n +
+          coverEntropyEntourage T univ V := by
+        rw [hmonoT.expGrowthSup_comp_mul hn.ne',
+          EReal.add_div_of_nonneg_right n.cast_nonneg']
+        congr 1
+        apply (EReal.div_eq_iff (EReal.natCast_ne_bot n)
+          (EReal.natCast_ne_top n) (Nat.cast_ne_zero.2 hn.ne')).2
+        exact mul_comm _ _
+      _ ≤ _ := add_le_add_right (coverEntropyEntourage_le_coverEntropy T univ hV) _
+  have hzero : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ENNReal.log (M : ℝ≥0∞) / n)
+      atTop (𝓝 (0 : EReal)) :=
+    EReal.tendsto_const_div_atTop_nhds_zero_nat hlog_bot hlog_top
+  have hlim : Tendsto
+      (fun n : ℕ => ENNReal.log (M : ℝ≥0∞) / n + coverEntropy T univ)
+      atTop (𝓝 (coverEntropy T univ)) := by
+    simpa only [Function.comp_def, zero_add] using
+      (EReal.continuousAt_add (p := (0, coverEntropy T univ))
+        (Or.inl EReal.zero_ne_top) (Or.inl EReal.zero_ne_bot)).tendsto.comp
+          (hzero.prodMk_nhds tendsto_const_nhds)
+  exact ge_of_tendsto hlim (by
+    filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop 1] with n hn
+    exact happrox n (by omega))
+

+/-- A continuous surjective semiconjugacy with a uniform finite bound on
+its fibers preserves topological entropy. The source dynamics is continuous;
+no continuity hypothesis on the factor dynamics is needed. -/
+theorem finite_fiber_entropy
+    {X Y : Type*} [UniformSpace X] [CompactSpace X]
+    [UniformSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] [T2Space Y]
+    (S : X → X) (T : Y → Y) (π : X → Y)
+    (hS : Continuous S) (hπ : Continuous π)
+    (honto : Surjective π) (hsem : Semiconj π S T)
+    (M : ℕ)
+    (hfib : ∀ y, (π ⁻¹' {y}).Finite ∧ (π ⁻¹' {y}).ncard ≤ M) :
+    coverEntropy S univ = coverEntropy T univ := by
+  classical
+  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty X with hX | hX
+  · letI := hX
+    letI : IsEmpty Y := ⟨fun y => by
+      obtain ⟨x, _⟩ := honto y
+      exact isEmptyElim x⟩
+    simp only [Set.eq_empty_of_isEmpty, coverEntropy_empty]
+  letI := hX
+  have hM : 0 < M := by
+    let x : X := Classical.arbitrary X
+    exact ((Set.ncard_pos (hfib (π x)).1).mpr ⟨x, by simp⟩).trans_le (hfib (π x)).2
+  apply le_antisymm
+  · unfold coverEntropy
+    refine iSup₂_le fun U hU => ?_
+    obtain ⟨W, hW, hWsymm, hWW⟩ := comp_symm_mem_uniformity_sets hU
+    letI := hWsymm
+    apply (coverEntropyEntourage_antitone S univ hWW).trans
+    apply entropy_le_of_block_bound S T (W ○ W) M hM
+    intro n hn
+    obtain ⟨V₀, hV₀, hlocal₀⟩ := local_block_covers π hπ S hS M hfib W hW n
+    obtain ⟨V, hV, hVsymm, hVV₀⟩ := symm_of_uniformity hV₀
+    letI := hVsymm
+    have hlocal : ∀ y, ∃ c : Finset X, c.card ≤ M ∧
+        IsDynCoverOf S (π ⁻¹' UniformSpace.ball y V) W n c := by
+      intro y
+      obtain ⟨c, hc, hcover⟩ := hlocal₀ y
+      exact ⟨c, hc, fun _ hx => hcover (hVV₀ hx)⟩
+    refine ⟨V, hV, fun r => ?_⟩
+    have hfinite := coverMincard_finite_of_isCompact_invariant
+      (T := T) isCompact_univ (mapsTo_univ T univ) hV (n * r)
+    obtain ⟨b, hb, hbcard⟩ := (coverMincard_finite_iff T univ V (n * r)).mp hfinite
+    obtain ⟨a, ha, hacard⟩ := block_cover_lift S T π hsem W V M n r hn hlocal b hb
+    calc
+      _ ≤ (a.card : ℕ∞) := ha.coverMincard_le_card
+      _ ≤ (b.card * M ^ r : ℕ) := by exact_mod_cast hacard
+      _ = (M : ℕ∞) ^ r * coverMincard T univ V (n * r) := by
+        rw [Nat.cast_mul, Nat.cast_pow, hbcard, mul_comm]
+  · have hfactor := coverEntropy_image_le_of_uniformContinuous hsem
+      (CompactSpace.uniformContinuous_of_continuous hπ) (Set.univ : Set X)
+    simpa only [Set.image_univ, Set.range_eq_univ.mpr honto] using hfactor
+
+#print axioms finite_fiber_entropy

+/- The two rational functions are restated locally so this general arithmetic
+result remains independent of the S0 certified counterexample layer. -/
+def f (n : ℕ) : ℚ :=
+  if n % 2 = 0 then (2 : ℚ) ^ ((1 : ℤ) - n) * n * (n - 1).choose (n / 2)
+  else (2 : ℚ) ^ ((1 : ℤ) - n) * n * (n - 1).choose ((n - 1) / 2)
+
+def g (n : ℕ) : ℚ :=
+  if n % 2 = 0 then 2 * (1 - (2 : ℚ) ^ (-(n : ℤ)) * n.choose (n / 2))
+  else 2 * (1 - (2 : ℚ) ^ (-(n : ℤ)) * n.choose ((n - 1) / 2))
+
+private theorem bounds_as_fractions (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
+    f n = (2 : ℚ) * ((n - n / 2 : ℕ) : ℚ) * n.choose (n / 2) / 2 ^ n ∧
+    g n = 2 * (1 - (n.choose (n / 2) : ℚ) / 2 ^ n) := by
+  have hk : (n - 1) / 2 = n / 2 ∨ n % 2 = 0 := by omega
+  have hbin : n * (n - 1).choose (n / 2) = n.choose (n / 2) * (n - n / 2) := by
+    simpa [Nat.sub_add_cancel hn, Nat.mul_comm] using
+      Nat.choose_mul_succ_eq (n - 1) (n / 2)
+  have hpow : (2 : ℚ) ^ ((1 : ℤ) - n) = 2 / (2 : ℚ) ^ n := by
+    rw [zpow_sub₀ (by norm_num), zpow_one, zpow_natCast]
+  have hneg : (2 : ℚ) ^ (-(n : ℤ)) = 1 / (2 : ℚ) ^ n := by simp
+  have hf : f n = (2 : ℚ) ^ ((1 : ℤ) - n) * n * (n - 1).choose (n / 2) := by
+    rcases hk with hk | hk <;> simp [f, hk]
+  have hg : g n = 2 * (1 - (2 : ℚ) ^ (-(n : ℤ)) * n.choose (n / 2)) := by
+    rcases hk with hk | hk <;> simp [g, hk]
+  constructor
+  · rw [hf, hpow]
+    have hc : (n : ℚ) * ((n - 1).choose (n / 2) : ℚ) =
+        (n.choose (n / 2) : ℚ) * ((n - n / 2 : ℕ) : ℚ) := by exact_mod_cast hbin
+    calc
+      _ = 2 * ((n : ℚ) * ((n - 1).choose (n / 2) : ℚ)) / 2 ^ n := by ring
+      _ = _ := by rw [hc]; ring
+  · rw [hg, hneg]; ring

+/-- For every positive `n`, the numerator of `g n` is the odd binomial gap `G`,
+and the only cancellation in the ratio is `gcd (ceil (n/2)) G`.
+Here `factorization B 2` is exactly the exponent of 2 in the positive binomial
+coefficient `B`; all divisions defining `b` and `G` are exact natural divisions. -/
+theorem denominator_formula (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
+    let m := n - n / 2
+    let B := n.choose (n / 2)
+    let v := B.factorization 2
+    let b := B / 2 ^ v
+    let G := (2 ^ n - B) / 2 ^ v
+    (g n).num = (G : ℤ) ∧
+      (f n / g n).den = G / Nat.gcd m G ∧
+      (f n / g n).num = ((m * b / Nat.gcd m G : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
+  dsimp only
+  let m := n - n / 2
+  let B := n.choose (n / 2)
+  let v := B.factorization 2
+  let b := B / 2 ^ v
+  let r := n - v
+  let G := 2 ^ r - b
+  have hB : 0 < B := Nat.choose_pos (Nat.div_le_self n 2)
+  have hBlt : B < 2 ^ n := Nat.choose_lt_two_pow n (n / 2) (by omega)
+  have hd : 2 ^ v ∣ B := Nat.ordProj_dvd B 2
+  have hdb : 2 ^ v * b = B := Nat.mul_div_cancel' hd
+  have hv : v < n := by
+    have hp : 2 ^ v ≤ B := Nat.le_of_dvd hB hd
+    exact (Nat.pow_lt_pow_iff_right (by norm_num : 1 < 2)).mp (lt_of_le_of_lt hp hBlt)
+  have hr : 0 < r := by dsimp [r]; omega
+  have hsplit : 2 ^ n = 2 ^ v * 2 ^ r := by rw [← pow_add]; congr 1; dsimp [r]; omega
+  have hb : 0 < b := Nat.ordCompl_pos 2 hB.ne'
+  have hblt : b < 2 ^ r := by
+    have h := hBlt
+    rw [← hdb, hsplit] at h
+    exact (Nat.mul_lt_mul_left (by positivity : 0 < 2 ^ v)).mp h
+  have hG : 0 < G := Nat.sub_pos_of_lt hblt
+  have hGdef : (2 ^ n - B) / 2 ^ v = G := by
+    rw [hsplit, ← hdb, ← Nat.mul_sub_left_distrib, Nat.mul_div_right _ (by positivity)]
+  have hb2 : Nat.Coprime b 2 := (Nat.coprime_ordCompl Nat.prime_two hB.ne').symm
+  have hbG : Nat.Coprime b G :=
+    (Nat.coprime_sub_self_right hblt.le).mpr (hb2.pow_right r)
+  have hdenpow : 2 ^ r = 2 * 2 ^ (r - 1) := by
+    rw [← pow_succ']; congr 1; omega
+  have hG2 : Nat.Coprime G 2 := by
+    apply Nat.coprime_two_right.mpr
+    apply (Nat.odd_sub' hblt.le).mpr
+    exact ⟨fun _ => by exact ⟨2 ^ (r - 1), by omega⟩,
+      fun _ => hb2.odd_of_right⟩
+  have hGpow : Nat.Coprime G (2 ^ (r - 1)) := hG2.pow_right _
+  obtain ⟨hf, hg⟩ := bounds_as_fractions n hn
+  have hdbq : (B : ℚ) = 2 ^ v * b := by exact_mod_cast hdb.symm
+  have hsplitq : (2 : ℚ) ^ n = 2 ^ v * 2 ^ r := by exact_mod_cast hsplit
+  have hGq : (G : ℚ) = 2 ^ r - b := by exact_mod_cast Nat.cast_sub hblt.le
+  have hg' : g n = (G : ℚ) / 2 ^ (r - 1) := by
+    rw [hg, hdbq, hsplitq, hGq]
+    have hpq : (2 : ℚ) ^ r = 2 * 2 ^ (r - 1) := by exact_mod_cast hdenpow
+    rw [hpq]
+    field_simp
+    <;> ring
+  have hratio : f n / g n = ((m * b : ℕ) : ℚ) / G := by
+    rw [hf, hg, hdbq, hsplitq, hGq]
+    simp only [Nat.cast_mul]
+    change (2 * (m : ℚ) * (2 ^ v * b) / (2 ^ v * 2 ^ r)) /
+      (2 * (1 - (2 ^ v * b) / (2 ^ v * 2 ^ r))) =
+      (m : ℚ) * b / (2 ^ r - b)
+    have hne : (2 : ℚ) ^ r - b ≠ 0 := by
+      rw [← hGq]; exact_mod_cast hG.ne'
+    field_simp [hne]
+    <;> ring
+  change (g n).num = (((2 ^ n - B) / 2 ^ v : ℕ) : ℤ) ∧
+    (f n / g n).den = ((2 ^ n - B) / 2 ^ v) / Nat.gcd m ((2 ^ n - B) / 2 ^ v) ∧
+    (f n / g n).num = ((m * b / Nat.gcd m ((2 ^ n - B) / 2 ^ v) : ℕ) : ℤ)
+  rw [hGdef, hratio]
+  constructor
+  · rw [hg']
+    rw [show (2 : ℚ) ^ (r - 1) = ((2 ^ (r - 1) : ℕ) : ℚ) by norm_cast,
+      Rat.natCast_div_eq_divInt, Rat.divInt_ofNat, Rat.num_mkRat]
+    simp [show 2 ^ (r - 1) ≠ 0 by positivity, hGpow.symm.gcd_eq_one]

+private theorem geometry {k t : ℕ} (hk : 3 ≤ k)
+    (hsmall : ∀ i : Fin k, |actualSource k t i| < quarter k →
+      0 < actualSource k t i) :
+    (∀ i, actualSource k t i ≠ 0) ∧
+    (∀ i, 0 < actualSource k t i → 3 * actualSource k t i ≤ modulus k) ∧
+    (∀ i, actualSource k t i < 0 →
+      quarter k ≤ -actualSource k t i ∧
+      actualSource k t (phase (by omega) i 1) = 2 * actualSource k t i + modulus k ∧
+      0 < actualSource k t (phase (by omega) i 1)) := by

+  let σ := fun i : Fin k => phase (by omega : 0 < k) i 1

+    change -half k ≤ w i ∧ w i ≤ half k at h

+    simpa [w, σ] using phase_step hk t i 0

+    intro h
+    have hh := hsmall i (by change |w i| < quarter k; rw [h]; norm_num; omega)
+    change 0 < w i at hh
+    omega
+  have neg (i : Fin k) (hi : w i < 0) :
+      quarter k ≤ -w i ∧ w (σ i) = 2 * w i + modulus k ∧ 0 < w (σ i) := by
+    have hl : quarter k ≤ -w i := by
+      by_contra hh
+      have hp := hsmall i (by change |w i| < quarter k; rw [abs_of_neg hi]; omega)
+      change 0 < w i at hp
+      omega
+    have ht := hs i

+      ite_eq_left (by omega : 4 * w i < -modulus k)] at ht

+    exact ⟨hl, ht, by omega⟩
+  have posStep (i : Fin k) (hi : quarter k ≤ w i) :

+    · exact ⟨σ i, (neg i (by have := hnz i; omega)).2.2⟩

+  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := existsPos
+  obtain ⟨a, ha, hmax⟩ := P.exists_max_image w ⟨i, (memP i).2 hi⟩
+  have hapos := (memP a).1 ha

+    by_contra hh
+    have ht := hs a
+    rw [doubleStep, ite_eq_right (by omega : ¬modulus k < 4 * w a),

+  have hm := hmax (σ (σ a)) ((memP _).2 hp)
+  refine ⟨hnz, ?_, neg⟩
+  intro j hj
+  have hmj := hmax j ((memP _).2 hj)
+  change 3 * w j ≤ modulus k
+  omega

+private theorem phase_add {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (a : Fin k) (i j : ℕ) :
+    phase hk (phase hk a i) j = phase hk a (i + j) := by
+  apply Fin.ext
+  simp only [phase]
+  rw [Nat.mod_add_mod, Nat.add_assoc]

+private theorem path_nodup {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (a : Fin k) (m : ℕ)
+    (hm : m ≤ k) : (path hk a m).Nodup := by
+  unfold path
+  refine List.Nodup.map_on ?_ List.nodup_range
+  intro i hi j hj he
+  have hi' : i < k := lt_of_lt_of_le (List.mem_range.mp hi) hm
+  have hj' : j < k := lt_of_lt_of_le (List.mem_range.mp hj) hm
+  have hh : Nat.ModEq k (a.val + i) (a.val + j) := congrArg Fin.val he
+  have hc := Nat.ModEq.add_left_cancel' a.val hh
+  simpa only [Nat.ModEq, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hi', Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hj'] using hc

+private theorem first_root {k t : ℕ} (hk : 3 ≤ k)
+    (a : Fin k) (ha : 0 < actualSource k t a) :
+    ∃ r : ℕ, quarter k ≤ actualSource k t (phase (by omega) a r) ∧
+      (∀ j < r, 0 < actualSource k t (phase (by omega) a j) ∧

+      (∀ j ≤ r, actualSource k t (phase (by omega) a j) =

+        (∀ j < r, 0 < actualSource k t (phase (by omega) a j) ∧
+          actualSource k t (phase (by omega) a j) < quarter k) ∧
+        (∀ j ≤ r, actualSource k t (phase (by omega) a j) =
+          (2 : ℤ) ^ j * actualSource k t a) := by

+        have hj0 : j = 0 := by omega

+        have hb : 0 < actualSource k t b := by dsimp [b]; omega
+        have hm : (quarter k - actualSource k t b).toNat < n := by
+          dsimp [b]
+          rw [hstep]
+          omega
+        obtain ⟨r, hr, hpre, hpow⟩ := ih _ hm b rfl hb
+        have hshift (j : ℕ) : phase (by omega) b j = phase (by omega) a (j + 1) := by
+          dsimp [b]
+          rw [phase_add]
+          congr 1 <;> omega
+        refine ⟨r + 1, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩

+        · intro j hj
+          cases j with
+          | zero => simp
+          | succ j =>
+            have ht := hpow j (by omega)
+            rw [hshift] at ht
+            rw [ht, show actualSource k t b = 2 * actualSource k t a from hstep, pow_succ]

+  exact aux _ a rfl ha

+/-- Initial segment before the first budget crossing, paired with its literal
+suffix. For positive weights this is the longest affordable prefix. -/
+def splitBudget {α : Type*} (f : α → ℤ) : ℤ → List α → List α × List α
+  | _, [] => ([], [])
+  | B, x :: xs => if f x ≤ B then
+      let z := splitBudget f (B - f x) xs
+      (x :: z.1, z.2)
+    else ([], x :: xs)
+
+/-- T is preceding mass; each occurrence remembers its birth height. -/
+def Ancestors {α : Type*} (f : α → ℤ) (mu D : ℤ) : ℤ → List α → Prop
+  | _, [] => True
+  | T, x :: xs => 0 ≤ f x - mu - T ∧ f x - mu - T ≤ D ∧
+      Ancestors f mu D (T + f x) xs
+
+private theorem ancestor_prefix {α : Type*} {f : α → ℤ} {mu D T : ℤ}
+    (q e : List α) (h : Ancestors f mu D T (q ++ e)) : Ancestors f mu D T q := by
+  induction q generalizing T with
+  | nil => trivial
+  | cons x xs ih => exact ⟨h.1, h.2.1, ih h.2.2⟩
+
+private theorem ancestor_suffix {α : Type*} {f : α → ℤ} {mu D T : ℤ}
+    (q e : List α) (h : Ancestors f mu D T (q ++ e)) :
+    Ancestors f mu D (T + (q.map f).sum) e := by
+  induction q generalizing T with
+  | nil => simpa using h
+  | cons x xs ih => simpa [add_assoc] using ih h.2.2
+
+private theorem ancestor_append {α : Type*} {f : α → ℤ} {mu D T : ℤ}
+    (q e : List α) (hq : Ancestors f mu D T q)
+    (he : Ancestors f mu D (T + (q.map f).sum) e) : Ancestors f mu D T (q ++ e) := by
+  induction q generalizing T with
+  | nil => simpa using he
+  | cons x xs ih =>
+    refine ⟨hq.1, hq.2.1, ih hq.2.2 ?_⟩
+    simpa [add_assoc] using he

+private theorem dyadic_ancestors {α : Type*} {f : α → ℤ} {mu D T a : ℤ}
+    {l : List α} (hl : Dyadic f a l) (hlo : 0 ≤ a - mu - T)

+    exact ih hl.2 (by rw [hl.1]; omega) (by rw [hl.1]; omega)

+private theorem split_spec {α : Type*} (f : α → ℤ) (B : ℤ) (l : List α)

+Classical bilinear normal-order calculation on the original finite-charge
+polynomial carrier. The current transpose is an explicit smaller supplier;
+no all-source adjointness, symmetry or nondegeneracy of the form is assumed.
+The normal product and divided derivative are the actual constructors of
+FieldNormalProduct, retaining their Carnahan/native adaptation attribution.
+The finite scalar cutoffs follow the structure of HalfFock.NormalScalarTranspose,
+with integer reflection k ↦ -k and a separate charge-sensitive zero boundary.
+The intended consumer is the cons step of the original wordField BPZ induction.

+/-- Order p corresponds to insertion h_i(-(p+1)). -/
+def insertion (D : LatticeData) (i : Fin D.rank) (p : ℕ)
+    (F : VertexOperator ℂ (Carrier D)) : VertexOperator ℂ (Carrier D) :=
+  (normalMinusOne (dividedDerivative p (neutralField D i)) F).1
+
+private def coefficient (p : ℕ) (k : ℤ) : ℂ :=
+  ((Ring.choose (-k-1) p : ℤ) : ℂ)
+
+private theorem derivative_mode (D : LatticeData) (i : Fin D.rank) (p : ℕ) (m : ℤ) :
+    ((dividedDerivative p (neutralField D i))[[m]]) =
+      coefficient p (m-p) • neutralMode D i (m-p) := by
+  apply LinearMap.ext
+  intro v
+  change Ring.choose (-m-1+p) p •
+    HVertexOperator.coeff (neutralField D i) (-m-1+p) v = _
+  rw [VertexOperator.coeff_eq_ncoeff, neutralField_ncoeff]
+  rw [show -(-m-1+p)-1 = m-p by omega]
+  simp only [coefficient, LinearMap.smul_apply, Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul]
+  congr 2; omega
+
+private theorem coefficient_zero_band (p : ℕ) (k : ℤ)
+    (hk : -(p : ℤ) ≤ k) (hn : k < 0) : coefficient p k = 0 := by
+  have ha : 0 ≤ -k-1 := by omega
+  obtain ⟨a, he⟩ := Int.eq_ofNat_of_zero_le ha
+  have hb : a < p := by omega
+  simp [coefficient, he, Ring.choose_natCast, Nat.choose_eq_zero_of_lt hb]

+private theorem coefficient_reflection (p : ℕ) (j : ℤ) :
+    -coefficient p (-j) = (-1 : ℂ)^(p+1) *
+      ∑ s ∈ Finset.range (p+1), ((p+1).choose (s+1) : ℂ) * coefficient s j := by
+  have h : Ring.choose (j-1) p = (-1 : ℤ)^p *
+      ∑ s ∈ Finset.range (p+1), ((p+1).choose (s+1) : ℤ) * Ring.choose (-j-1) s := by
+    rw [show j-1 = -(-j+1) by ring, Ring.choose_neg]
+    rw [show (-j+1)+(p : ℤ)-1 = (-j-1)+((p+1 : ℕ) : ℤ) by push_cast; ring]
+    rw [Ring.add_choose_eq p (Commute.all _ _),
+      Finset.Nat.sum_antidiagonal_eq_sum_range_succ_mk]
+    simp only [Units.smul_def, zsmul_eq_mul, Int.cast_negOnePow_natCast]
+    congr 1
+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro s hs
+    have hs' : s ≤ p := Nat.le_of_lt_succ (Finset.mem_range.mp hs)
+    rw [Ring.choose_natCast, ← Nat.choose_symm (by omega : p-s ≤ p+1),
+      show p+1-(p-s) = s+1 by omega]
+    ring
+  have hc := congrArg (fun z : ℤ => (z : ℂ)) h
+  push_cast at hc
+  simp only [coefficient, neg_neg]
+  rw [hc, pow_succ]
+  ring

+private theorem coefficient_at_zero (p : ℕ) :

+  simp only [coefficient, neg_zero, zero_sub]
+  rw [show (-1 : ℤ) = -(1 : ℤ) by rfl, Ring.choose_neg]
+  simp [Units.smul_def, Ring.choose_natCast]

+private theorem forward_finite (D : LatticeData) (L F : VertexOperator ℂ (Carrier D))
+    (m : ℤ) (u : Carrier D) :
+    Function.HasFiniteSupport (fun t : ℕ => (L[[-(t : ℤ)-1]]) ((F[[m+t]]) u)) := by
+  refine BddAbove.finite (bddAbove_def.mpr ?_)
+  refine ⟨(-((HahnModule.of ℂ).symm (F u)).order-m).toNat, ?_⟩
+  intro t ht
+  contrapose! ht
+  have hz : (F[[m+t]]) u = 0 := by
+    apply VertexOperator.ncoeff_eq_zero_of_lt_order
+    omega
+  simp [hz]

+private theorem reverse_finite (D : LatticeData) (L F : VertexOperator ℂ (Carrier D))
+    (m : ℤ) (u : Carrier D) :
+    Function.HasFiniteSupport (fun t : ℕ => (F[[m-t-1]]) ((L[[t]]) u)) := by
+  refine BddAbove.finite (bddAbove_def.mpr ?_)
+  refine ⟨(-((HahnModule.of ℂ).symm (L u)).order-1).toNat, ?_⟩
+  intro t ht
+  contrapose! ht
+  have hz : (L[[t]]) u = 0 := by
+    apply VertexOperator.ncoeff_eq_zero_of_lt_order
+    omega
+  simp [hz]

+private def cutoff (D : LatticeData) (u : Carrier D) : ℕ :=
+  vectorFrequencyBound D u + 1
+
+private theorem cutoff_pos (D : LatticeData) (u : Carrier D) : 0 < cutoff D u := by
+  simp [cutoff]
+
+private theorem cutoff_vanish (D : LatticeData) (i : Fin D.rank) (u : Carrier D)
+    (k : ℤ) (hk : (cutoff D u : ℤ) ≤ k) : neutralMode D i k u = 0 := by
+  apply neutralMode_vanish
+  dsimp [cutoff] at hk
+  omega

+private theorem scalar_offsets (D : LatticeData) (B : LinearMap.BilinForm ℂ (Carrier D))
+    (i : Fin D.rank)
+    (hB : ∀ k x y, B (neutralMode D i k x) y = -B x (neutralMode D i (-k) y))
+    (p : ℕ) (F : VertexOperator ℂ (Carrier D)) (m : ℤ) (u v : Carrier D) :
+    B (((insertion D i p F)[[m]]) u) v =
+      (∑ t ∈ Finset.range (cutoff D v),
+        coefficient p (-(t : ℤ)-1-p) *
+          B (neutralMode D i (-(t : ℤ)-1-p) ((F[[m+t]]) u)) v) +
+      ∑ t ∈ Finset.range (cutoff D u+p),
+        coefficient p ((t : ℤ)-p) *
+          B ((F[[m-t-1]]) (neutralMode D i ((t : ℤ)-p) u)) v := by
+  let L := dividedDerivative p (neutralField D i)
+  rw [insertion, (normalMinusOne L F).2]
+  change (B.flip v) (_+_) = _
+  rw [map_add, map_finsum (B.flip v) (forward_finite D L F m u),
+    map_finsum (B.flip v) (reverse_finite D L F m u)]
+  simp only [L, derivative_mode, LinearMap.smul_apply, LinearMap.BilinForm.flip_apply,
+    map_smul, smul_eq_mul]

+      omega

+  · apply finsum_eq_sum_of_support_subset
+    intro t ht

+    by_contra ho
+    have hz : neutralMode D i ((t : ℤ)-p) u = 0 := by
+      apply cutoff_vanish
+      omega
+    exact ht (by dsimp only; simp [hz])

+      ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 0 ((cutoff D u : ℤ)-1),

+      (∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 0 ((cutoff D v : ℤ)-1), -coefficient p (-j) * right j)) +
+        (-1 : ℂ)^(p+1) * κ * B u ((G[[H]]) v) := by
+    rw [hl, hr, Finset.sum_insert (by simp), Finset.sum_insert (by simp)]
+    rw [neg_zero, coefficient_at_zero, hz, pow_succ]
+    ring

+  have hsum :
+      (∑ s ∈ Finset.range (p+1), ((p+1).choose (s+1) : ℂ) *
+        ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc (1-(cutoff D u : ℤ)) (-1), coefficient s j * left j) +
+      (∑ s ∈ Finset.range (p+1), ((p+1).choose (s+1) : ℂ) *
+        ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 0 ((cutoff D v : ℤ)-1), coefficient s j * right j) =

+/-- Finite original scalar insertion law. Here n=p+1, and the summation index
+s=r-1 runs through 0,...,p. The last summand deletes the inserted oscillator.
+Only the smaller current law, a finite tail transpose, and its zero-mode charge
+covariance are premises. In particular the all-source BPZ law is not a premise. -/
+theorem consumed_normal_product_form (D : LatticeData)
+    (B : LinearMap.BilinForm ℂ (Carrier D)) (i : Fin D.rank)
+    (hB : ∀ k x y, B (neutralMode D i k x) y = -B x (neutralMode D i (-k) y))
+    (p : ℕ) (F : VertexOperator ℂ (Carrier D))

+    (weight : σ → ℂ) (K : σ → ℤ) (κ : ℂ)
+    (htail : ∀ t x y, B ((F[[t]]) x) y =
+      ∑ a ∈ S, weight a * B x (((G a)[[K a - t]]) y))
+    (hzero : ∀ a ∈ S, ∀ t x, neutralMode D i 0 (((G a)[[t]]) x) =
+      ((G a)[[t]]) (neutralMode D i 0 x) + κ • ((G a)[[t]]) x)
+    (m : ℤ) (u v : Carrier D) :
+    B (((insertion D i p F)[[m]]) u) v =
+      (-1 : ℂ)^(p+1) * ∑ a ∈ S, weight a *
+        ((∑ s ∈ Finset.range (p+1), ((p+1).choose (s+1) : ℂ) *
+          B u (((insertion D i s (G a))[[K a+p+s+2-m]]) v)) +
+          κ * B u (((G a)[[K a+p+1-m]]) v)) := by
+  classical

+      ∑ a ∈ S, weight a * (-coefficient p k *
+        B u (((G a)[[K a+p+1-m+k]]) (neutralMode D i (-k) v))) := by
+    rw [hB, htail, ← Finset.sum_neg_distrib, Finset.mul_sum]
+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro a ha
+    rw [show K a-(m-k-p-1) = K a+p+1-m+k by omega]
+    ring
+  have positive (k : ℤ) :
+      coefficient p k * B ((F[[m-k-p-1]]) (neutralMode D i k u)) v =
+      ∑ a ∈ S, weight a * (-coefficient p k *
+        B u (neutralMode D i (-k) (((G a)[[K a+p+1-m+k]]) v))) := by
+    rw [htail, Finset.mul_sum]
+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro a ha
+    rw [hB, show K a-(m-k-p-1) = K a+p+1-m+k by omega]
+    ring

+    Finset.sum_comm (s := Finset.Icc 0 ((cutoff D u : ℤ)-1)) (t := S),
+    ← Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.mul_sum]

+  intro a ha

+      B u (((G a)[[K a+p+1-m+k]]) (neutralMode D i (-k) v)))
+      (1-(cutoff D v : ℤ)) (-1),
+    reflect_interval (fun k => -coefficient p k *
+      B u (neutralMode D i (-k) (((G a)[[K a+p+1-m+k]]) v)))
+      0 ((cutoff D u : ℤ)-1)]
+  simp only [neg_neg, neg_zero,
+    show -(1-(cutoff D v : ℤ)) = (cutoff D v : ℤ)-1 by omega,
+    show -((cutoff D u : ℤ)-1) = 1-(cutoff D u : ℤ) by omega,
+    show ∀ j : ℤ, K a+p+1-m+-j = (K a+p+1-m)-j by intro j; omega]

+  have hm : ∀ s : ℕ, K a+p+1-m+s+1 = K a+p+s+2-m := by intro s; omega
+  simp only [hm]
+  ring
+

+
+## Verified locator

+- DOI: https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9947-1971-0274707-X (Crossref identifies *Transactions of the American Mathematical Society*, volume 153, pages 401–414, published 1971).
+- The DOI and bibliographic fields were checked against the Crossref work record. No theorem, equation, or page-specific claim is attributed to Bowen beyond the general factor-entropy context stated below.
+
+Bowen's article appeared in Transactions of the American Mathematical Society,
+volume 153 (1971), pp. 401–414. This reference acknowledges the classical
+factor-entropy framework; no novelty is claimed for entropy preservation by
+uniformly finite-to-one compact factors.
+
+The repository proves its exact compact-uniform-space statement independently:
+a continuous surjective semiconjugacy, continuous source dynamics, Hausdorff
+target, and an explicit uniform natural-number bound on finite fibers imply
+equality of covering entropy. Its block-cover construction bounds the lift
+cost over r blocks by M^r and sends the entropy cost log(M)/n to zero.

 ## 追加锚（本行以下为增补区）
+## 73. 活跃代码交换下的联合 Born 刚性与全扇区泄漏边界
+
+**定义 73.1（完整响应与活跃代码合同）。** 保留定义 70.1 的十站点合法路径扇区 $H$、初态 $J|0,0\rangle=|1000100010\rangle$、地址字母表 $K_0,\ldots,K_6$、正向有限制备字 $W$、完整输出集
+
+$$
+\Omega_{10}=\{0,1\}^{10},\qquad \psi_W=WJ|0,0\rangle .
+$$
+
+令
+$P:S(H)\to\Delta(\Omega_{10})$
+为一个连续、全局相位不变且支撑保持的响应：
+
+$$
+P_w(e^{i\gamma}\psi)=P_w(\psi),\qquad
+\psi_w=0\Longrightarrow P_w(\psi)=0 .
+\tag{73.1}
+$$
+
+这里的单纯形假设只是普通的非负、归一化终端概率；它不解释概率为何存在。对每个有限 $W$ 假设原定义 70.1 的 Alice-$b_1$ 无信号条件
+
+$$
+\sum_{w:b_1=0}P_w(\psi_W)
+ =\sum_{w:b_1=0}P_w(K_5\psi_W).
+\tag{73.2}
+$$
+
+在代码坐标 $1=00,2=01,3=10,4=11$ 上定义
+
+$$
+p_i(\xi)=P_{J i}(J\xi),\qquad \xi\in\mathbb C^4,\quad \|\xi\|_2=1 .
+$$
+
+另加一个明确的活跃校准假设：对每个 $\pi\in S_4$ 和每个归一代码向量，
+
+$$
+p(\pi\xi)=\pi p(\xi).
+\tag{73.3}
+$$
+
+这里的 $\pi$ 是固定探测器标签上的响应函数等式，不是把被动标签重命名冒充为物理上已经执行的幅度交换门。假设 (73.3) 只在 $J(\mathbb C^4)$ 上量化。
+
+**定理 73.2（K5 加活跃 $S_4$ 的代码域联合响应刚性）。** 在定义 73.1 的条件下，(73.2) 与 (73.3) 蕴含
+
+$$
+p_i(\xi)=|\xi_i|^2\qquad(i=1,2,3,4)
+\tag{73.4}
+$$
+
+对每个归一 $\xi\in\mathbb C^4$ 成立。结论只涉及代码内四个输出；它不蕴含 $P$ 在其余 $1020$ 个输出或整个可达扇区上是 Born 响应。证明只使用 Bob 的 $I$ 与 $K_5$ 两个终端设置；$K_4$ 仍是制备字母表中的地址，但不需要另加为终端设置。
+
+**证明。** 写 $\xi=(u,v)\in\mathbb C^2\oplus\mathbb C^2$，其中 $u=(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ 是 $b_1=0$ 行，$v=(\xi_3,\xi_4)$ 是 $b_1=1$ 行，并置
+
+$$
+F(\xi)=p_1(\xi)+p_2(\xi),\qquad q_i=|\xi_i|^2 .
+$$
+
+由 (70.3)，任意代码向量 $J\xi$ 都有定义 70.1 的有限字列 $\psi_{W_n}$ 以整体相位收敛到它。连续性、(73.1) 以及 $K_5$ 的酉性把 (73.2) 延伸为
+
+$$
+F(T\xi)=F(\xi),\qquad T=K_Q\oplus K_Q,
+\tag{73.5}
+$$
+
+其中 $K_Q$ 是 (70.4) 的实际原生二维块。这个极限保留完整的 $1024$ 个输出；没有丢弃码外振幅，也没有把剩余概率重新归一。支撑保持只在理想代码向量上使码外概率为零，故此处 $\sum_{i=1}^4p_i=1$。更具体地，令完整事件差为
+
+$$
+D(\psi)=\sum_{w:b_1=0}P_w(K_5\psi)-\sum_{w:b_1=0}P_w(\psi).
+$$
+
+若 $\Delta=D(J\xi)=F(T\xi)-F(\xi)\ne0$，连续性给出 $J\xi$ 的邻域，使 $|D(\psi)-\Delta|<|\Delta|/2$。因此该邻域内 $D(\psi)$ 与 $\Delta$ 同号，且 $|D(\psi)|>|\Delta|/2$。由全局相位不变性和 (70.3)，某个实际有限正向字 $W$ 落入此相位对齐的邻域，给出同号严格差值。这只使用 $P$ 的连续性，不使用未知响应的 Born 误差界。
+
+令 $X=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$，并令
+
+$$
+A=X\oplus I_2,\qquad B=I_2\oplus X .
+$$
+
+由 (73.3) 的换位 $(12)$、$(34)$，分别有 $F(A\xi)=F(\xi)$ 与 $F(B\xi)=F(\xi)$。把块对 $(g,h)$ 与 $g\oplus h$ 识别，取实际矩阵生成的闭群
+
+$$
+\mathcal H=\overline{\langle (K_Q,K_Q),(X,I_2),(I_2,X)\rangle}
+ \ \subseteq U(2)\times U(2).
+$$
+
+这里 $\det X=-1$，所以两个换位确实属于所写的 $U(2)$ 因子。$F$ 对每个生成元不变；在任意单位向量上代入其逆像，便得对逆的不变性；逐次应用及连续性给出对整个 $\mathcal H$ 的不变性。
+
+以下直接在该群内取得独立的行作用。记 $\sigma_x=X$、$\sigma_y=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$、$\sigma_z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$。由实际原生块 (70.4) 及 $\zeta^5=-1$、$\zeta^{10}=1$，
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+E:=K_Q^5&=2Q-I_2=n_x\sigma_x+n_z\sigma_z,\\
+n_x&=2x^{3/2},\qquad n_z=2x-1,\qquad x=\varphi^{-1},\\
+n_x^2+n_z^2&=1,\qquad n_xn_z\ne0.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{73.6}
+$$
+
+因此 $E^2=I_2$，$E$ 为酉反射且 $\det E=-1$。置 $C=EXEX=(EX)^2$。因为 $EX$ 酉且行列式为一，$C\in SU(2)$；并有精确群字
+
+$$
+T^5AT^{-5}A=C\oplus I_2,\qquad
+T^5BT^{-5}B=I_2\oplus C .
+$$
+
+这是同一 $T=K_Q\oplus K_Q$ 的五次幂与 (73.3) 所给代码坐标换位的组合，没有单独把任何一行的 $X$ 换成 $iX$。令
+
+$$
+N_1=\{g\in SU(2):g\oplus I_2\in\mathcal H\}.
+$$
+
+它是闭子群，且含有 $C$。由 $EX=n_xI_2+i n_z\sigma_y$ 和 $x^2+x=1$，
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+C&=(n_x^2-n_z^2)I_2+2i n_xn_z\sigma_y,\\
+\operatorname{tr}C&=4n_x^2-2=16x^3-2=32x-18=16\sqrt5-34.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+该迹的代数共轭为 $-16\sqrt5-34<-2$。v15 引理 4.1 因而给出 $C$ 无限阶；其两个本征值的本征轴由上式及 $n_xn_z\ne0$ 确定，所以
+
+$$
+\overline{\langle C\rangle}
+ =\{\exp(it\sigma_y):t\in\mathbb R\}\subseteq N_1 .
+$$
+
+用 $T\in\mathcal H$ 共轭第一行的这个圆，仍在 $N_1$ 中。设 $\alpha=3\pi/5$；从 $K_Q=\zeta[I+(\zeta-1)Q]$ 直接相乘得到
+
+$$
+K_Q\sigma_yK_Q^*
+ =\cos\alpha\,\sigma_y
+   +\sin\alpha\,(n_z\sigma_x-n_x\sigma_z).
+$$
+
+因为 $\sin\alpha\ne0$ 且 $n_x^2+n_z^2=1$，$i\sigma_y$ 与 $iK_Q\sigma_yK_Q^*$ 在 $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ 中实线性无关。v15 引理 4.2 遂给出 $N_1=SU(2)$：这两个圆的生成元及其非零交换子张成 $\mathfrak{su}(2)$。对第二个精确群字使用相同论证，得到 $N_2=\{g\in SU(2):I_2\oplus g\in\mathcal H\}=SU(2)$；两个块作用相乘，故 $SU(2)\times SU(2)\subseteq\mathcal H$。
+
+因此 $F$ 在两行上分别具有独立的 $SU(2)$ 不变性。具体地，对单位列 $h=(h_0,h_1)^T$，矩阵 $U_h=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}h_0&-\overline h_1\\h_1&\overline h_0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\in SU(2)$ 把 $(1,0)^T$ 送到 $h$；这证明每个固定范数的复二维球面上传递，包括两向量只差相位的情形。零行无需选择方向。于是定义连续函数 $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ 为 $f(t)=F(\sqrt t,0,\sqrt{1-t},0)$，支撑保持及归一化给出
+
+$$
+F(\xi)=f(q_1+q_2),\qquad f(0)=0,\quad f(1)=1 .
+\tag{73.7}
+$$
+
+最后用 (73.3) 把同一式传到任意二元子集：对任意不同的 $i,j$，
+
+$$
+p_i(\xi)+p_j(\xi)=f(q_i+q_j).
+\tag{73.8}
+$$
+
+取 $\xi=(\sqrt a,\sqrt b,\sqrt{1-a-b},0)$，其中 $a,b\ge0$ 且 $a+b\le1$。支撑保持给出 $p_4=0$，所以 (73.8) 的子集 $\{1,4\}$、$\{2,4\}$ 和 $\{1,2\}$ 分别给出
+
+$$
+ p_1=f(a),\qquad p_2=f(b),\qquad f(a+b)=f(a)+f(b).
+\tag{73.9}
+$$
+
+非负性使 $f$ 单调；有理等分给出 $f(m/n)=m/n$，连续性再给 $f(t)=t$。于是所有二元和为 $q_i+q_j$，并对互异的 $i,j,k$ 有
+
+$$
+2p_i=(p_i+p_j)+(p_i+p_k)-(p_j+p_k)=2q_i .
+$$
+这就得到 (73.4)，也包括零坐标和单位端点。证毕。
+
+**推论 73.3（非 Born 代码响应的实际有限见证）。** 取定义 73.1 中除 (73.2) 外的全部响应、来源及菜单假设，特别保留连续性、全局相位不变性、支撑保持、完整 $1024$ 输出，以及对每个 $\pi\in S_4$ 和每个归一复代码向量成立的活跃协变 (73.3)。若代码上存在 $\xi$ 和 $i$ 使 $p_i(\xi)\ne|\xi_i|^2$，则存在字母表 $\{K_0,\ldots,K_6\}$ 上的实际有限正向制备字 $W$（允许空字），使
+
+$$
+\sum_{w:b_1=0}P_w(K_5\psi_W)
+ \ne\sum_{w:b_1=0}P_w(\psi_W).
+$$
+
+见证的字、长度和边缘间隙可依赖于 $P$；不存在由本推论给出的统一字长、统一间隙或有限样本认证。证明是定理 73.2 对“每个有限正向字 $W$ 均满足 (73.2)”的逆否命题。等价地，若所有理想代码向量的 $D(J\xi)$ 都为零，上述群论与可加性论证就给出代码 Born 律；故非 Born 响应必有某个 $\Delta=D(J\xi)\ne0$，再由 (73.5) 后的连续性论证返回同号、绝对值大于 $|\Delta|/2$ 的实际有限见证。
+
+**命题 73.4（既有 72.1 扰动不满足活跃交换）。** §72.1 的矩阵扰动在其余假设下保持边缘，但不满足 (73.3)。取
+
+$$
+M=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
+q_{ab}=\frac14,\qquad |\det M|^2=\frac14,\qquad
+\tau=\frac{\lambda}{1024}>0 .
+$$
+
+交换代码坐标 $00$ 与 $01$ 时，振幅向量本身不变，而 (72.1) 的两个响应值为
+
+$$
+\widetilde P_{00}=\frac14+\tau,\qquad
+\widetilde P_{01}=\frac14-\tau .
+$$
+
+因此左侧 $p((12)\xi)=p(\xi)$，右侧 $(12)p(\xi)$ 却交换了两个不等值分量，活跃协变式失败。这个检验也说明被动标签重命名不能替代固定探测器上的主动幅度交换假设。

+**命题 73.5（较弱的行分块对称边界）。** 令
+
+$$
+G_{\rm row}=\{\pi\in S_4:\pi(\{1,2\})\in\{\{1,2\},\{3,4\}\}\},
+$$
+
+这是保留行分块 $\{1,2\}|\{3,4\}$ 的八元素群。对 $0<\lambda<1$，在每一行的无序对 $\{i,j\}$ 上定义
+
+$$
+ p_i=q_i+\lambda q_iq_j(q_i-q_j),\qquad
+ p_j=q_j-\lambda q_iq_j(q_i-q_j).
+\tag{73.10}
+$$
+
+两行分别使用同一公式。该响应连续、归一化、支撑保持、$G_{\rm row}$-协变，并保持两行和 $p_1+p_2=q_1+q_2$、$p_3+p_4=q_3+q_4$；但一般不等于 $q$。非负性来自
+$p_j\ge q_j(1-\lambda q_i)\ge0$
+及对称情形。故行分块稳定子不足以得到联合刚性；这里给出的是一个精确较弱对称边界，不主张任何普遍的最小子群结论。
+
+**命题 73.6（完整 $1024$ 输出的代码外反例）。** 在同一合法路径扇区上取两个输出字
+
+$$
+ u=1000000010,\qquad v=1000100010=J|0,0\rangle,

+
+它们均有 Alice 位 $b_1=0$，且 $u$ 在代码外。对任意归一 $\psi\in S(H)$ 写 $q_w(\psi)=|\psi_w|^2$，固定 $0<\lambda<1$，令

+## 4. Past-visible resets and the actual future-measure comparison
+
+**Definition 4.1 (Past-visible finite-context class).** Let $N\ge1$ and let $\theta=(\lambda,M_0,M_1)$ range over the entire domain
+
+$$
+\lambda\ge0,\quad\lambda\mathbf1=1,\quad M_0,M_1\ge0,\quad
+A=M_0+M_1,\quad A\mathbf1=\mathbf1,\quad\lambda A=\lambda,\quad
+\lambda M_1^2\mathbf1=0.
+\tag{4.1}
+$$
+
+Use the actual stationary joint law of [R, Definition 8.1][R], with hidden states $H_i$ immediately before emission at $i$:
+
+$$
+J_\theta(H_a=h_a,\ldots,H_{b+1}=h_{b+1},X_a=x_a,\ldots,X_b=x_b)
+=\lambda_{h_a}\prod_{i=a}^bM_{x_i}(h_i,h_{i+1}).
+\tag{4.2}
+$$
+
+Write $P=P_\theta$ for its visible marginal. Structural zeros, zero stationary hidden masses, reducibility, periodicity and redundant states are allowed. The last condition in (4.1) is scalar; it does not impose $M_1^2=0$ on the whole matrix. Require $\iota=P(X_0=1)>0$, occupied anchors unbounded in both spatial directions, and a finite nonempty context set $C$. At every occupied anchor $t$, let
+
+$$
+C_t=D^-((X_{t-j})_{j\ge1})
+\tag{4.3}
+$$
+
+for one fixed measurable strict-left decoder. These marks extend (4.2) to a stationary marked law $J$. In its actual Palm law $Q=J(\,\cdot\mid X_0=1)$ enumerate anchors by $T_0=0$, $T_k<T_{k+1}$, and set $G_k=T_{k+1}-T_k\ge2$, $C_k=C_{T_k}$. Require
+
+$$
+0<\mu=\mathbb E_QG_0<\infty,\qquad
+C_{k+1}=\tau_{G_k}(C_k),\qquad
+\mathcal L_Q(H_{T_k+1}\mid\mathcal H_k)=r_{C_k},
+\quad
+\mathcal H_k=\sigma(C_j:j\le k;G_j:j<k),
+\tag{4.4}
+$$
+
+for every $k\in\mathbb Z$, where $\tau_g:C\to C$ are arbitrary maps and $r_c$ are probability rows on the original hidden state set. Conditions on a context of zero Palm mass are void. No strict-right context decoder is assumed. This class is defined by (4.1)–(4.4), separately from Definition 1.1.
+
+The objective remains the original one: for legal words $B_n=\{w\in\{0,1\}^n:w_iw_{i+1}=0\}$, let $\Gamma_n$ have all legal Hamming-one edges with open endpoints, $h(s,t)=st/(s+t)$ for $s+t>0$ and $h(0,0)=0$, and
+
+$$
+\Phi_n(\pi)=\sum_{\{u,v\}\in E(\Gamma_n)}h(\pi_u,\pi_v),\qquad
+\kappa_n=\max_{\pi\in\mathcal P(B_n)}\Phi_n(\pi),\qquad
+c_\star=\lim_n\kappa_n/n.
+\tag{4.5}
+$$
+
+For the entire exterior $\mathcal E_i=\sigma(X_j:j\ne i)$ choose a Borel version $q_0=\mathbb E_P[X_0\mid\mathcal E_0]\in[0,1]$, and put $q_i=q_0\circ T^i$ for $(Tx)_j=x_{j+1}$. The actual risk is
+
+$$
+d(P)=\mathbb E_P(X_0-q_0)^2\le c_\star.
+\tag{4.6}
+$$
+
+These are [R, §1][R] and [U, §1][U]'s same open-path objective and full-exterior risk, including zero masses and forced fibers.
+
+**Proposition 4.2 (Actual rows and recurrent conditional laws).** Suppose Definition 4.1 holds and $d(P)=c_\star$. Put $\nu_c=Q(C_0=c)$ and $C_+=\{c:\nu_c>0\}$. Every $c\in C_+$ has a normalized finite-mean row
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+f_c(g)&=Q(G_0=g\mid C_0=c)=r_cM_0^{g-1}M_1\mathbf1
+\ge 2^{-(g+1)}/3\quad(g\ge2),\\
+Q(G_k=g,C_{k+1}=b\mid\mathcal H_k)
+&=f_{C_k}(g)\mathbf1_{\{b=\tau_g(C_k)\}}.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{4.7}
+$$
+
+In particular, with $\alpha_c=r_cM_0$, $T_0=M_0$ and $b_0=M_1\mathbf1$,
+
+$$
+f_c(k+2)=\alpha_cT_0^kb_0,\qquad
+\alpha_c\mathbf1=1,\qquad T_0\mathbf1+b_0=\mathbf1.
+\tag{4.8}
+$$
+
+The positive contexts split into closed irreducible classes $D$ of
+
+$$
+K(c,b)=\sum_{g\ge2}f_c(g)\mathbf1_{\{b=\tau_g(c)\}},\qquad\nu K=\nu.
+\tag{4.9}
+$$
+
+Each class is closed under every $\tau_g$. Its label is spatially invariant and belongs to every strict-left half-line and every exterior field. Conditioning on a class preserves (4.7), (4.8), the original posterior versions and attainment.
+
+Proof. At a Palm anchor, past gaps recover every visible coordinate strictly to its left: their cumulative sums enumerate all preceding occupied sites. Conversely the strict-left decoder recovers every past mark from those coordinates. Thus $\mathcal H_0$ and the visible past at the known anchor agree modulo actual Palm null sets. The path Markov property of (4.2), followed by conditional expectation using (4.4), gives the conditional future cylinders $r_{C_0}M_w\mathbf1$. This proves (4.7) at zero; Palm event stationarity, obtained by the anchor-counting identity [R, (35.2)][R], transports it to all integer event indices. No negative-index stopping-time assertion is needed. Almost-sure next-anchor existence gives normalization. Since $\nu_c>0$ and $\mathbb E_QG_0<\infty$, each row mean is finite. The proof of Proposition 1.2 uses only (4.3) and the attained exterior comparison [U, Theorem 3.1][U], so its lower bound applies here. No11 gives $r_cM_1\mathbf1=0$, hence (4.8).
+
+Event stationarity gives (4.9). A stationary finite stochastic matrix gives zero mass to transient states; positivity of $\nu$ on $C_+$ and of every $f_c(g)$ proves the asserted closed-class decomposition. The class label is constant along anchors. It can be read from an anchor arbitrarily far to the left, so its event $E_D$ belongs to every exterior $\mathcal E_i$ and is invariant under site shifts. The actual conditional laws are stationary and their Palm laws are exactly $Q(\,\cdot\mid C_0\in D)$. Moreover $P(E_D)\ge\iota\nu(D)>0$ and $\mathbb E_{Q(\cdot\mid D)}G_0\le\mu/\nu(D)$. Conditional expectation on an $\mathcal E_i$-measurable component shows that the same $q_i$ is its posterior. Therefore
+
+$$
+d(P)=\sum_D P(E_D)d(P(\,\cdot\mid E_D)),
+\tag{4.10}
+$$
+
+and the upper bound $c_\star$ for each summand forces attainment in each positive component. The class event already belongs to $\mathcal H_k$, so the actual reset and full-history rule also survive conditioning. $\square$
+
+**Proposition 4.3 (Comparison of entire future measures).** Fix one component $D$ of Proposition 4.2 and use its conditional law. Let $F_c$ be the law on $\{2,3,\ldots\}^{\mathbb N_0}$ of the entire future gap sequence starting at a context-$c$ anchor. For $c\in D$ and $l,r\ge2$, put
+
+$$
+M=f_c(l+r),\quad B=f_c(l)f_{\tau_l(c)}(r),\quad
+ a=\tau_{l+r}(c),\quad b=\tau_r(\tau_l(c)).
+$$
+
+As measures on the entire future after the right exterior anchor,
+
+$$
+\frac M3F_a\ \le\ B F_b\ \le\ M F_a.
+\tag{4.11}
+$$
+
+Proof. Specify the nearest exterior anchors at $-l,r$, the strict-left context $c$ at $-l$, and a measurable future-gap event $E$ after $r$. Conditional independence of the full future from the full past given $c$ follows by iterating (4.7) and a monotone-class argument. The center-zero and center-one external subprobability measures, including any full-left-past test, factor respectively as
+
+$$
+\iota_D\nu^D_c M\,\kappa_c^-\otimes F_a,
+\qquad
+\iota_D\nu^D_c B\,\kappa_c^-\otimes F_b.
+\tag{4.12}
+$$
+
+Here $\kappa_c^-$ is the actual conditional left-past channel and $\iota_D,\nu^D$ are the actual conditional intensity and Palm row. Apply the exterior mass comparison (1.5) to these external tests and cancel the positive common scalar and left channel. This proves (4.11) for every measurable $E$. It gives mutual absolute continuity, not equality, of $F_a,F_b$. $\square$
+
+## 5. The spatial absolute-continuity phase and finite synchronization
+
+**Proposition 5.1 (Predictive quotient and labelled-graph phase).** In a fixed component of Proposition 4.2, first identify contexts having equal entire future laws. The resulting finite state set $S$ has distinct laws $F_s$, well-defined rows $f_s$ and maps $\tau_g$. Next identify states when $F_s$ and $F_t$ are mutually absolutely continuous. On this second quotient the labelled maps are
+
+$$
+\bar\tau_g=U^g\quad(g\ge2)
+\tag{5.1}
+$$
+
+for one cyclic permutation $U$. Thus its classes can be labelled $\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z$ so that an edge with gap $g$ adds $g$. This quotient is a strongly connected labelled graph; it need not carry a common probability row within a phase. No lumpability of the original $K$ is asserted.
+
+Proof. Equality of future laws implies equality of their first-gap probabilities. Conditioning on any first gap $g$, whose mass is positive, then gives equality of the successor future laws. This constructs the first quotient and its rows. The same conditioning argument shows that mutual absolute continuity passes to successors, so it defines the second quotient's maps. Equation (4.11) gives
+
+$$
+\bar\tau_{l+r}=\bar\tau_r\bar\tau_l\quad(l,r\ge2).
+\tag{5.2}
+$$
+
+The quotient labelled graph is strongly connected because the original component is irreducible and every label has positive probability at every state. Relation (5.2) makes its maps commute. For each $g$, the nonempty image of $\bar\tau_g$ is invariant under all labelled maps. Strong connectivity forces this image to be the whole quotient, so every map is a permutation. Set $A_2=\bar\tau_2$, $A_3=\bar\tau_3$. Then $A_3^2=A_2^3$ and $U=A_3A_2^{-1}$ has $U^2=A_2$, $U^3=A_3$. Relation (5.2), starting with $2,3$, gives (5.1) for every $g\ge2$. Strong connectivity now makes $U$ a single cycle. This is the finite-map algebra of [V, Theorem 57.1][V], applied to labelled maps rather than to representative phase rows. $\square$
+
+**Proposition 5.2 (Two half-line decoders for phase and invariant component).** Write $A_t$ for the absolute-continuity phase at an occupied anchor $t$. For any site $i$ define
+
+$$
+S_i=A_t+i-t\pmod m
+\tag{5.3}
+$$
+
+using a preceding anchor $t<i$. This is independent of the chosen anchor and has both strict-left and strict-right visible decoders. Every invariant component label $E_D$ also belongs to both strict half-lines. These assertions concern only phase and component, not the original contexts or the predictive states inside a phase.
+
+Proof. Formula (5.1) gives anchor independence and $S_{i+1}=S_i+1$. The preceding anchor and its strict-left mark make $S_i$ strictly past measurable. On the stationary component let $\zeta=e^{2\pi\mathrm i/m}$ and $Z=e^{2\pi\mathrm i S_0/m}$. Then
+
+$$
+Z\circ T^n=\zeta^n Z.
+\tag{5.4}
+$$
+
+Finite-past conditional expectations $Z_n=\mathbb E[Z\mid X_{-n},\ldots,X_{-1}]$ tend to $Z$ in $L^2$. The functions $\zeta^{-(n+1)}Z_n\circ T^{n+1}$ depend only on $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ and their distances from $Z$ in $L^2$ equal $\|Z_n-Z\|_2$ by stationarity and (5.4). The future-measurable subspace of $L^2$ is closed; hence $Z$, and therefore $S_0$, has a Borel strict-future version. Countably many shifts give the decoder at every actual anchor. For an invariant component indicator $Z=\mathbf1_{E_D}$ the identical argument uses eigenvalue $1$ under the unconditioned law. Thus component labels are future measurable as well as past measurable. This eigenvalue-$1$ case is also valid when $m=1$. $\square$
+
+**Proposition 5.3 (A common finite word merges each phase).** For a finite normalized deterministic predictive automaton with distinct future laws and strictly positive rows on the countable gap alphabet, there is a nonempty finite word $w$ that merges every pair in each mutual-absolute-continuity class:
+
+$$
+\tau_w(s)=\tau_w(t)\quad\text{whenever }F_s\sim F_t.
+\tag{5.5}
+$$
+
+Here $\tau_v=\tau_{g_k}\cdots\tau_{g_1}$ and
+
+$$
+L_s(v)=\prod_{j=1}^k f_{\tau_{g_{j-1}}\cdots\tau_{g_1}s}(g_j)
+\quad(v=(g_1,\ldots,g_k)),\qquad L_s(\varnothing)=1.
+\tag{5.6}
+$$
+
+The conditional probability of $w$ from any state is at least $\varepsilon=\min_s L_s(w)>0$. For disjoint trials of its $k$ gaps, failure in the first $n$ trials has probability at most $(1-\varepsilon)^n$ after any actual event history.
+
+Proof. On the finite ordered unequal-pair set define the substochastic matrix
+
+$$
+W_{(s,t),(u,v)}=
+\sum_{\substack{g\ge2:\tau_gs=u,\ \tau_gt=v\\u\ne v}}
+\sqrt{f_s(g)f_t(g)}.
+\tag{5.7}
+$$
+
+Cauchy–Schwarz bounds every row sum by $1$. If $\rho(W)=1$, a finite substochastic matrix has a nonempty closed stochastic irreducible class: otherwise every final communicating class loses mass, and every state reaches such a loss, forcing a power to have row sums below $1$. At a row of a closed stochastic class equality in Cauchy–Schwarz gives $f_s(g)=f_t(g)$ for all $g$. Positivity and closure ensure that every positive-symbol successor pair remains unequal in that class. Induction gives $L_s(v)=L_t(v)$ for every finite word $v$, hence $F_s=F_t$, contrary to predictive minimality. Therefore $\rho(W)<1$.
+
+If a pair has no merging word, every word from it stays unequal, and the Hellinger affinity of its length-$n$ prefix laws is exactly $(W^n\mathbf1)_{(s,t)}$, tending to zero. To identify the full-measure limit, dominate both laws by $\eta=(F_s+F_t)/2$. The densities of their restrictions to the prefix fields are the conditional expectations $p_n=\mathbb E_\eta[dF_s/d\eta\mid\mathcal F_n]$, $q_n=\mathbb E_\eta[dF_t/d\eta\mid\mathcal F_n]$. They are bounded by $2$ and converge almost surely to the full densities because the prefix fields generate the gap space. Dominated convergence gives
+
+$$
+\lim_n\int\sqrt{p_nq_n}\,d\eta
+=\int\sqrt{(dF_s/d\eta)(dF_t/d\eta)}\,d\eta.
+\tag{5.8}
+$$
+
+Zero affinity means singularity. Consequently an equivalent pair must have a merging word.
+
+Start with an empty common word. Whenever an original same-class pair still has unequal images, those images still have equivalent future laws; append one of their merging words. Equal images cannot separate under later symbols, so each step eliminates at least one of finitely many original pairs. This terminates with (5.5). If all classes were already singletons, any one-symbol word suffices. Countable alphabet size causes no zero-word problem: every selected finite word has a finite product of positive probabilities, and there are only finitely many initial states. The conditional failure bound follows by iterating the uniform lower bound $\varepsilon$ on successive trials.
+
+The pair-graph synchronization method is related to Travers–Crutchfield, *Exact Synchronization for Finite-State Sources*, [§II.4, Definition 5; §III.1, Theorem 1; §IV.1, Definitions 11–12 and Theorem 3](https://arxiv.org/html/1008.4182). Their stated alphabet is finite. The argument (5.7)–(5.8) supplies the countable-gap, within-phase version needed here, without invoking a finite-alphabet theorem outside its hypotheses. $\square$
+
+**Proposition 5.4 (Entire-exterior posterior from a finite future prefix).** Under the attainment hypothesis of Proposition 4.2, consider a free exterior cell $F_0=\{X_{-1}=X_1=0\}$ with nearest anchors $-l,r$ and left context $c$. With $M,B,a,b$ as in Proposition 4.3, any finite observed future gap prefix $v$ after $r$ containing an intact copy of $w$ gives the original posterior
+
+$$
+q_0=\frac{B L_b(v)}{M L_a(v)+B L_b(v)}.
+\tag{5.9}
+$$
+
+On the forced complement $F_0^c$, $q_0=0$.
+
+Proof. The competing states $a,b$ have the same absolute-continuity phase by (4.11). Before the copy of $w$ their successors remain in the same phase, and after it their minimal predictive states coincide, say at $u$. On the prefix cylinder the full future laws factor as $L_a(v)F_u$ and $L_b(v)F_u$. In (4.12) both the common full-left-past channel and this common entire-future tail cancel, proving (5.9) by disintegration on the entire exterior field. This is not a quotient of point masses at infinite configurations. The geometric trial bound makes these prefix cylinders cover almost every future. Countably many prefixes, contexts, distances and spatial shifts admit a common conull formula domain. No right decoder for $c$, $a$ or $b$ is used. $\square$
+
+## 6. Physical guard tails and both original erasure fields
+
+**Proposition 6.1 (Exponential physical waiting lengths).** For each fixed component in Proposition 4.2, gaps and the physical waiting length to a completed copy of $w$ have a positive exponential moment at an anchor, uniformly over its finitely many predictive states. There are constants $C<\infty$, $\beta>0$, depending on the producer and component, such that the probability that a stationary spatial interval of length $j$ contains no complete guard is at most $Ce^{-\beta j}$. The same bound holds for negative spatial intervals.
+
+Proof. In (4.8), telescoping gives
+
+$$
+\alpha_cT_0^n\mathbf1
+=1-\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\alpha_cT_0^kb_0\longrightarrow0.
+\tag{6.1}
+$$
+
+Restrict $T_0$ to the finite survival states reachable from $\alpha_c$. A reachable closed class with no absorption would give positive eternal-survival probability, contradicting (6.1). The restricted substochastic matrix therefore has spectral radius below $1$, so its powers decay exponentially. This proves $\sum_g e^{tg}f_c(g)<\infty$ for some $t>0$. The finite row family permits one common positive $t$; the predictive quotient uses the same rows. Neither full-matrix transience nor a reverse-time transition rule is needed.
+
+Let $k$ be the number of gaps in $w$, $Y=G_0+\cdots+G_{k-1}$ the physical trial length, and $S_k$ its final predictive state. Define
+
+$$
+D_t(s,u)=\mathbb E_s[e^{tY}\mathbf1_{\{(G_0,\ldots,G_{k-1})\ne w,\ S_k=u\}}],
+\quad
+h_t(s)=\mathbb E_s[e^{tY}\mathbf1_{\{(G_0,\ldots,G_{k-1})=w\}}].
+\tag{6.2}
+$$
+
+Iterated conditioning and the finite row moments make these finite and continuous at $t=0$ for small $t\ge0$. Since $\|D_0\|_\infty\le1-\varepsilon$, choose $t>0$ with $\|D_t\|_\infty<1$. The exponential moment of the physical length through the first successful disjoint trial is the convergent geometric sum
+
+$$
+\sum_{n\ge0}D_t^nh_t.
+\tag{6.3}
+$$
+
+A guard at a stationary origin is reached by first reaching the next anchor and then using (6.3). Palm inversion [R, (11.7)][R] weights a gap of length $g$ by $g/\mu$ and chooses its spatial offset. Its forward residual thus has an exponential moment at any smaller positive exponent, because $g e^{t'g}\le C_t e^{tg}$ when $0<t'<t$. The bound on (6.3) is uniform in the state reached there; integrating it gives an exponential stationary waiting tail. Completion within a window supplies a whole guard inside it. Translation invariance sends the event of no complete guard in a positive interval to that for a negative interval of equal length. This uses stationarity, not a reverse Markov assumption. $\square$
+
+**Proposition 6.2 (Exact retained-field estimators and root summability).** Under Definition 4.1 and $d(P)=c_\star$, use exactly
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\mathcal L_j&=\sigma(X_{-j},\ldots,X_{-1},X_1,X_2,\ldots),\\
+\mathcal R_j&=\sigma(\ldots,X_{-2},X_{-1},X_1,\ldots,X_j),\\
+p_j^L&=\mathbb E_P[X_0\mid\mathcal L_j],\quad
+p_j^R=\mathbb E_P[X_0\mid\mathcal R_j],\\
+e_L(j)&=\mathbb E_P(q_0-p_j^L)^2,\quad
+e_R(j)=\mathbb E_P(q_0-p_j^R)^2\qquad(j\ge0).
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{6.4}
+$$
+
+There are producer-dependent $K<\infty$, $\gamma>0$ such that
+
+$$
+e_L(j)+e_R(j)\le Ke^{-\gamma j},\qquad
+A_P=\sum_{j\ge0}\bigl(\sqrt{e_L(j)}+\sqrt{e_R(j)}\bigr)<\infty.
+\tag{6.5}
+$$
+
+Proof. Work first in a component. For $j\ge1$ both fields retain the two nearest neighbors, so a forced center has the exactly known posterior zero. On a free exterior, define the $\mathcal L_j$ good event by the existence of a complete guard with both endpoints in $[-j,-1]$. Choose its first such occurrence by a fixed spatial ordering. The entire retained future determines the component and spatial phase by Proposition 5.2; transport that phase to the guard's starting anchor. Proposition 5.3 makes its ending predictive state the common image of all states in that phase. All subsequent observed past gaps then transport this state to the nearest left anchor. The entire retained future supplies the nearest right anchor and a prefix containing another guard. Formula (5.9), now using the recovered left predictive state, is $\mathcal L_j$ measurable and equals $q_0$ on this event. Define $\widehat q_j^L$ by this formula on the good free event and by zero elsewhere, including forced configurations. Every selection uses countably many measurable word tests.
+
+For $\mathcal R_j$, the entire retained past directly gives the left context, component and phase. Its good free event is the existence of a complete guard with endpoints in $[1,j]$. Take the future prefix from the nearest right anchor through this guard. All of it is retained, so (5.9) defines an $\mathcal R_j$-measurable $\widehat q_j^R=q_0$ there; again set the estimator to zero off the good free event. A guard starting at the nearest right anchor is allowed. Thus both estimators are defined on their whole retained fields, with values in $[0,1]$.
+
+Because these fields are subfields of $\mathcal E_0$, the tower property gives $p_j^L=\mathbb E[q_0\mid\mathcal L_j]$ and its right analogue. Projection optimality and boundedness give
+
+$$
+e_L(j)\le\mathbb E(q_0-\widehat q_j^L)^2
+\le P(\text{no complete guard in }[-j,-1]),
+\qquad
+e_R(j)\le P(\text{no complete guard in }[1,j]).
+\tag{6.6}
+$$
+
+Proposition 6.1 bounds both terms exponentially. Enlarging the constant includes $j=0$, where each field still retains its entire opposite half-line and each defect is at most $1$.
+
+For the original finite mixture, Proposition 5.2 with eigenvalue $1$ places every $E_D$ in both retained fields, including at $j=0$. Consequently each conditional projection restricts to its component projection. With $\omega_D=P(E_D)$ the mixing identities are exactly
+
+$$
+e_L(j)=\sum_D\omega_D e_{L,D}(j),\qquad
+ e_R(j)=\sum_D\omega_D e_{R,D}(j).
+\tag{6.7}
+$$
+
+There are finitely many positive components. Taking the least of their positive rates and summing their constants proves the first assertion in (6.5). Finally,
+
+$$
+A_P\le2\sqrt K\sum_{j\ge0}e^{-\gamma j/2}
+=\frac{2\sqrt K}{1-e^{-\gamma/2}}<\infty.
+\tag{6.8}
+$$
+
+This is the original one-sided root sum, not a two-sided window error or a hidden-state recovery error. $\square$

+## 7. Same-law strong zero, inclusive guarded identities and a restricted exclusion
+
+**Proposition 7.1 (Saturated original-loss identities).** Under Definition 4.1 and $d(P)=c_\star$, put $\ell_i(x)=(x_i-q_i(x))^2$. There is one shift-invariant conull domain $\Omega$ saturated under all legal finite changes on which
+
+$$
+\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}(\ell_i(x)-\ell_i(z))=0
+\tag{7.1}
+$$
+
+absolutely for every $x,z\in\Omega$ differing at finitely many sites. In a fixed component, preserve a complete guard $w$ before the changed interval, a second complete guard after it, and a third after the second. If $A$ is the first guard's starting anchor and $B$ the second guard's ending anchor, then
+
+$$
+\sum_{i=A}^{B}\left[(x_i-q_i(x))^2-(z_i-q_i(z))^2\right]=0.
+\tag{7.2}
+$$
+
+Both boundary anchors are included. Each posterior in (7.2) is expressible using finitely many row entries and the predictive state at an unchanged preceding anchor. These are necessary rational-function identities for all compatible finite guarded patterns and legal fillings having the same physical endpoint length.
+
+Proof. Proposition 6.2 proves $A_P<\infty$ for the same actual $P$. Hence [Strong-zero, Definition 1.4 and Theorem 1.5](FIB_LEGAL_EDGE_LOAD_ATTAINMENT_STRONG_ZERO_EQUIVALENCE_AND_FINITE_OPTIMIZER_COMPARISON.md) applies with the unchanged original versions $q_i$ and losses $\ell_i$. It supplies (7.1) on a saturated conull set.
+
+For completeness, one can choose this domain to carry all the preceding formulas simultaneously. Intersect the structural and formula conull sets over every integer shift, then with the strong-zero domain and with every preimage under a legal replacement of a finite word on a finite integer interval. There are countably many such maps and their finite compositions. They are nonsingular: the attained band gives positive conditional mass to every legal single-site alternative, and deleting to zero then inserting a compatible word connects every legal finite fiber; iterated exterior comparisons preserve null sets. Thus the intersection is still conull and is saturated. Past-decoded component and phase are unchanged by a finite modification, since they can be recovered arbitrarily far to its left. This defines one $\Omega$ carrying original posterior formulas at both $x$ and every modified $z$.
+
+Before $A$, the first intact guard lies wholly after a scored center. It merges the two competing-center predictive paths, so (5.9) cancels all future information beyond that guard. The intervening unchanged coordinates and original left state are the same for $x,z$; hence $q_i(x)=q_i(z)$ for $i<A$. After the changed interval, equal physical displacement gives equal phases at the start of the second guard, regardless of the possibly different predictive states there. That guard merges their actual states. For $i>B$ the same state at $B$ and the unchanged later coordinates give the same left predictive channel and the same entire future, hence equal posteriors. Since the visible bits also agree outside the changed interval, every loss difference outside $[A,B]$ vanishes. This proves (7.2) from (7.1).
+
+For a scored center in $[A,B]$, including an occupied boundary anchor, deleting that center may break either of the first two guards. The third guard is intact in both center completions and lies strictly after the scored interval. Starting from an unchanged anchor preceding $A$, propagate the two finite completions through that third guard and use (5.9); on a forced fiber use zero. This computes each original $q_i$ by finite positive likelihoods, even at $A$ and $B$, and proves that the summands are rational functions of finitely many $f_s(g)$ values.
+
+Finally choose any positive starting state and any compatible guarded finite word. Every required finite gap word has positive probability by (4.7); compatible equal-length fillings have mutually absolutely continuous future channels after the second guard, where their states agree. The preceding starting state and phase have positive actual mass. The scalar expression in (7.2) is constant on this finite pattern with that starting state, independently of the more distant exterior. Its almost-sure zero value therefore forces the same scalar identity for every such pattern and filling. This argument asserts neither unconditional locality on all legal configurations nor a Gibbs specification. $\square$
+
+**Proposition 7.2 (Singleton absolute-continuity classes).** If every absolute-continuity class in each recurrent minimal predictive component of Definition 4.1 is a singleton, then $d(P)<c_\star$.
+
+Proof. Suppose equality held. In each positive component the phase of Proposition 5.1 is now the minimal predictive state itself. Proposition 5.2 supplies both strict half-line decoders for this state; Proposition 4.2 supplies its actual normalized positive finite-mean rows, full-history rule and finite absorption representations. Equal predictive laws have equal rows, so choosing any representative of a predictive state gives the same row and a representation (4.8). Thus the same actual conditional law satisfies [R, Definitions 11.1 and 12.1][R], with actual Palm weights and spatial transport $s\mapsto s+g$. The all-cycle exclusions used in Theorem 3.1 apply: [R, Theorem 4.3][R] for one phase; Theorems 16.2, 17.2 for two and three; Corollary 18.2 and Theorems 19.1, 20.1 for four; Theorems 21.2, 30.5, 31.1 for five through seven; and Theorem 32.1 for at least eight. Every positive conditional law would have risk strictly below $c_\star$, contradicting (4.10). The restriction to singleton classes is essential to this application. $\square$
